summary: Giorgio Renato Franci was an Indology, linguistics, and philosophy scholar. He studied under Luigi Heilmann at the University of Bologna (~1951–1956) and later held a post there from ~1961 to 2008.

Giovanni Gentile was a philosopher who studied at the Scuola Normale Superiore and the universities of Florence and Pisa. He held posts at Palermo, Pisa, and Sapienza University of Rome, and directed the Scuola Normale Superiore and Bocconi University.

Giovanni Vacca worked in Sinology, history, and archaeology. After earning a doctorate at the University of Genoa (~1893–1897) and studying at Florence (~1905–1908), he taught at the University of Florence (1910) and Sapienza University of Rome (1911–1948).

Giovanni Verardi is an archaeologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Allahabad, BHU, and Gorakhpur. He held posts at Ca' Foscari (1972–1987), Bologna (1981–1987), and Naples "L'Orientale" (1988–1993), alongside visiting professorships abroad.
Girijesh Dhar Dwivedi is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He completed an Acharya at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (2010–2011) and pursued a Ph.D. at SunRise University (2019–2026).

Girindrasekhar Bose studied at Presidency University, Calcutta Medical College, and the University of Calcutta. He served at Calcutta Medical College (1911–1915), the University of Calcutta as professor of experimental psychology (1917–1949), and presided over the Indian Psychoanalytic Society.

Girish Nath Jha works in Indology, linguistics, and computational fields. He was appointed professor at Jawaharlal Nehru University in 2002 and is attested as a retired professor of Sanskrit at Patna University (2009–2023).

Girolamo Donati was an Indologist who studied under Angelo De Gubernatis, succeeding him in 1890. He served as conservator at the Museo Indiano and was libero docente di sanscrito at the University of Florence (~1891–1901).

Gisbert Combaz, active in Sinology, history, and archaeology, studied law at Université libre de Bruxelles and trained under Louis de La Vallée Poussin. He taught at Ixelles, Université Nouvelle de Bruxelles (1905), and Académie Royale des Beaux-Arts (1912).

Gisela Emma Full, a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar, studied at the universities of Würzburg and Münster. She held research fellowships attested in 2013 at European University Viadrina and the Samueli Institute.

Gisela Freund was a historian and archaeologist who studied at the German University of Prague (~1939–1944). She served as head of the Department of Prehistory at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg from ~1969 to 1987.

Gisho Nakano was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Junjirō Takakusu at the University of Tokyo and obtained a doctorate from Kyushu University. He held posts at Peking University and served as professor and president of Koyasan University.
Giti Dutt is an archaeology and history researcher attested in 2026 as a PhD student at Australian National University under the doctoral supervision of Assa Doron.
Giulia Porru was a linguist and Indologist who earned her Ph.D. under Giacomo Devoto at the University of Florence (~1933–1937), where she was later appointed to teach Germanic philology in 1946.
Giuliana Martini is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts in 2010 at Kyoto University and the Italian School of East Asian Studies.

Giuliana Stramiglioni was a Japanologist who studied under Giuseppe Tucci (~1932–1936). She held a post at Naples (1938), taught Italian at the University of Tokyo (~1953–1965), and served as professor of Japanese at Sapienza University of Rome (1965–1985).

Giuseppe Bardelli was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied under Giuseppe Caspar Mezzofanti, Eugène Burnouf, and Stanislas Julien. He held teaching posts at the University of Pisa (1843, 1849–1851, 1862) and the University of Florence (1859–1862).

Giuseppe Caspar Mezzofanti was a linguist who held professorships in Hebrew, Oriental languages, and Ancient Greek at the University of Bologna between 1797 and 1831. He also served as Custodian-in-Chief at the Vatican Library from 1833.

Giuseppe De Lorenzo was a Buddhist studies and geology scholar who studied at the University of Naples Federico II (~1889–1894) and was a disciple of Karl Eugen Neumann. He served as professor at Naples from 1905 to 1941.
Giuseppe Maria da Gargnano was a religious studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Sapienza University of Rome and served as vice-prefect of the Tibet Mission in 1758.
